_help: Local flavor for the gamer on each box score page. Knobs are described in mac/gamer.py (FLAVOR_HELP). Only write what you know is true; lines may use {winner} {loser} {home} {away} {town} {floor}.

lines.text: Akron basketball dates to 1901, when the school was still Buchtel College and lost its first game to Mount Union, 120-9.
Akron's 1986 NCAA tournament trip under Bob Huggins ended with the 15th-seeded Zips losing 70-64 to second-seeded Michigan in Minneapolis.
Akron has made eight Division I NCAA tournament appearances, the first in 1986 and the most recent as a No. 12 seed against Texas Tech in 2026.
Before attaining Division I status in 1980, Akron twice reached the NCAA Division II national title game, finishing as runner-up to Evansville in 1964 and to Roanoke in 1972.
Akron joined the Mid-American Conference in 1992 after stops in the Ohio Valley Conference and the Mid-Continent Conference and a stretch as an independent.
Akron's 79-76 win over Toledo in the 2026 final made the Zips the first team in MAC tournament history to win three straight championships.
Joe Jakubick remains Akron's career scoring leader with 2,583 points, scored from the 1980-81 season through 1983-84.
The Akron single-game scoring record belongs to Jimond Ivey, who put up 48 points against Ball State in the 2017-18 season.
Zeke Marshall blocked 368 shots for Akron from 2009 to 2013, a school record, and owns the three highest single-season block totals in program history.
Akron's honored jerseys include Joe Jakubick's No. 31, Romeo Travis's No. 24, Enrique Freeman's No. 25 and Isaiah Johnson's No. 23.
Tony Laterza, who coached Akron from 1960 to 1968, went 178-59 for a .751 winning percentage that is still the best in program history.
Akron was founded in 1825 at the summit of the Ohio and Erie Canal, and its name comes from a Greek word meaning summit.
Akron, the seat of Summit County, sits about 40 miles south of Cleveland and counted 190,469 residents in the 2020 census.
Akron was nicknamed the Rubber Capital of the World as the home of Goodyear, Firestone, B.F. Goodrich and General Tire, and Goodyear is still based in the city.
Akron's Derby Downs has hosted the All-American Soap Box Derby each year since 1936, including its World Championship finals.
The University of Akron offered the world's first rubber chemistry courses in 1909 and opened the first College of Polymer Science and Polymer Engineering in 1988.
The University of Akron was founded in 1870 as Buchtel College, named for industrialist John R. Buchtel, and became a state university in 1967.
Akron's nickname came from a 1927 campus contest, when student Margaret Hamlin suggested Zippers after a rubber overshoe sold by the city's B.F. Goodrich Co.
Akron's teams were the Zippers until 1950, when athletic director Kenneth Cochrane shortened the name to Zips.
Akron's mascot, Zippy, is a female kangaroo accepted by the student council on May 1, 1953, and won the Capital One Bowl mascot competition for the 2007 season.
Akron's fight song, The Akron Blue and Gold, was written by bandleader Fred Waring and premiered on an NBC broadcast on Nov. 17, 1939.
Akron's student section, the AK-Rowdies, started in 2005 with fewer than 100 members backing the men's basketball team and grew to more than 1,000.
Enrique Freeman left Akron with a school-record 1,405 rebounds and went to the Indiana Pacers with the 50th pick of the 2024 NBA draft, the first Zip drafted since 1987.
Enrique Freeman tied the NCAA single-season record with 31 double-doubles for Akron in 2023-24, averaging 18.6 points and 12.9 rebounds.
Akron native Keith Dambrot, who coached LeBron James for two seasons at St. Vincent-St. Mary High School, won a school-record 305 games in 13 seasons leading the Zips.
Akron native Romeo Travis, the first Zip named MAC Player of the Year, led Le Mans Sarthe Basket to the French league title in 2018.
Dustin Ford is in his first season as Akron's 23rd head coach after nine seasons as the Zips' associate head coach under John Groce.
Akron coach Dustin Ford started all four seasons as a player at Ohio and later helped coach the Bobcats to the 2012 Sweet 16.
Akron went 29-6 last season and made the NCAA tournament for the third straight year.
Akron was picked third in the MAC preseason poll behind Miami and Toledo and opened the season No. 7 in the CollegeInsider.com Mid-Major Top 25.
Akron's Evan Mahaffey and Tahj Staveskie were both named to the Preseason All-MAC Second Team.
Akron spends Thanksgiving week in Kissimmee, Florida, at the ESPN Events Invitational, playing Nov. 23-25 in a six-team group with Appalachian State, Belmont, St. Bonaventure, Wright State and Yale.
Akron opens MAC play on Dec. 2 against Ball State at James A. Rhodes Arena.
Akron and the rest of the MAC's top eight teams will meet in the conference tournament March 10-13 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland.
Akron and rival Kent State meet twice this season, Feb. 13 in Kent and March 5 in Akron in the regular-season finale for the Zips.
Akron and Kent State first met in basketball in the 1915-16 season, when Akron won 37-16 at Kent State.
The Akron-Kent State Wagon Wheel traces to a legend that Akron industrialist John R. Buchtel lost a wagon wheel in the mud in Kent in the spring of 1870 while scouting a site for a college.

home_lines: Another night at the JAR, James A. Rhodes Arena, in the Rubber City.

home_lines.text: James A. Rhodes Arena, known in Akron as the JAR, opened on Dec. 3, 1983, cost $12.5 million and seats 5,500.
All 5,500 seats at Akron's James A. Rhodes Arena are retractable, with 1,323 armchair seats on the lower level, 773 on the west-side upper level and bleachers for the rest.
The JAR sits at 373 Carroll Street in Akron and is named for former Ohio governor Jim Rhodes.
In the early 2000s the JAR in Akron hosted some home games for LeBron James and his St. Vincent-St. Mary High School team.
Akron won the 1986 Ohio Valley Conference tournament on its own floor at James A. Rhodes Arena, beating Middle Tennessee 68-63 in the final.
Akron's James A. Rhodes Arena was built next to the university's 3,000-seat Memorial Hall and replaced it as home of the Zips when it opened in 1983.

lines.text: Kent State's first intercollegiate basketball game was a 56-6 loss to Otterbein on Jan. 22, 1915.
Kent State, seeded 13th, beat fourth-seeded Indiana in the first round of the 2001 NCAA Tournament in San Diego.
Kent State reached the Elite Eight in 2002 as a No. 10 seed, beating Oklahoma State, Alabama and Pittsburgh before an 81-69 loss to Indiana.
The 2001-02 Kent State team went 30-6, won 21 straight games, finished 17-1 in the Mid-American Conference and was ranked 12th in the final ESPN/USA Today coaches poll.
Kent State has won seven Mid-American Conference tournament titles, in 1999, 2001, 2002, 2006, 2008, 2017 and 2023.
Kent State has won six MAC regular-season championships, in 2002, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2011 and 2015.
Kent State's 2024-25 team won NIT road games at St. Bonaventure and Stanford before losing at Loyola Chicago in the quarterfinals.
Kent State's first postseason victory came against Rutgers in the 2000 NIT, a tournament in which the Golden Flashes reached the quarterfinals.
Kent was known as Franklin Mills until 1864, when the town was renamed in honor of Marvin Kent.
Kent is nicknamed the Tree City because of the Davey Tree Expert Company, which is headquartered there and is the city's largest private employer.
Kent, a city of 28,215 in the 2020 census, is on the Cuyahoga River about 10 miles northeast of Akron and 30 miles southeast of Cleveland.
An extension of Kent State's University Esplanade, completed in October 2013, links the campus with downtown Kent.
Acorn Alley, a pedestrian alleyway lined with small shops in downtown Kent, opened in 2009.
The black squirrels on the Kent State campus were brought there from Canada in 1961 by the university's head groundskeeper.
Kent State's first nickname, in 1923, was the Silver Foxes, for a silver fox ranch next to campus, before a Name the Team contest later that decade produced Golden Flashes.
Kent State legend holds that the school's original orange and blue basketball uniforms came back from the laundry gold and blue, and the new colors stuck.
Kent State's eagle mascot, Flash, emerged from a fiberglass egg at halftime of the 1985 homecoming game.
After wins, Kent State teams sing the fight song and then ring the Starner Victory Bell, a gift from two alumni.
Antonio Gates averaged 20.6 points and scored 640 points as a Kent State senior before becoming a three-time first-team All-Pro tight end with the San Diego Chargers.
Jim Christian went 138-58 as Kent State's coach from 2002 to 2008, a span in which the Golden Flashes won MAC Tournament titles in 2006 and 2008.
Rob Senderoff became the winningest coach in Kent State history on Dec. 28, 2018, when his 149th victory moved him past Jim McDonald.

Rob Senderoff, a native of Spring Valley, N.Y., was a Kent State assistant from 2002 to 2006 and 2008 to 2011, with two seasons at Indiana in between, before being hired as head coach on April 7, 2011.
Kent State went 24-10 last season and finished third in the Mid-American Conference at 14-4.
Kent State is coming off back-to-back NIT appearances, reaching the quarterfinals in 2025 and losing in the first round in 2026.
Kent State and Akron meet twice this season, on Feb. 13 at the M.A.C. Center and on March 5 at Akron in the regular-season finale.
Akron entered this season with an 89-83 lead in its all-time series with Kent State, including an 8-4 edge in MAC Tournament meetings.

Kent State and Akron play football for the Wagon Wheel, which legend ties to Akron industrialist John R. Buchtel, whose wagon is said to have gotten stuck in 1870 where the Kent State campus now sits.
Kent State and Akron compete in the Wagon Wheel Challenge, a yearlong competition across 16 sports in which the first school to earn 8.5 points wins.

home_lines.text: Kent State opened its arena on Dec. 2, 1950, with a 51-46 upset of Pittsburgh before about 4,000 fans.
Kent State's M.A.C. Center on Risman Drive seats 6,327 for basketball.
The largest crowd to watch a game in Kent State's arena was 7,778 for a visit from St. Bonaventure on Jan. 10, 1970.
Kent State's arena opened as the Men's Physical Education Building, was Memorial Gymnasium from 1956 to 1991 and became the Memorial Athletic and Convocation Center in November 1991.
A renovation of Kent State's arena from 1990 to 1992 replaced the building's swimming pool with a three-story entrance lobby.
LeBron James played in Kent State's arena as a high schooler with Akron's St. Vincent-St. Mary in December 2001.
The Eagles played a concert in Kent State's gym on May 3, 1975, with general admission tickets priced at $5.50.
The largest crowd at Kent State's M.A.C. Center since its 1992 renovation was 6,567 for a game against Akron on March 4, 2007.

lines.text: Toledo's program record for wins in a season is 27, set in 2013-14 and matched in 2022-23, the same season the Rockets put together a school-record 17-game winning streak.
Toledo won four consecutive outright MAC regular-season championships from 2020-21 through 2023-24.
Tod Kowalczyk, who came to Toledo in 2010 after eight seasons at Green Bay, went 315-211 in his first 16 seasons with the Rockets and had 451 career wins as a head coach through 2025-26.
Tod Kowalczyk, the MAC Coach of the Year at Toledo in 2020-21 and 2022-23, still holds the single-game scoring record at De Pere High School in Wisconsin with 53 points.

home_lines: Savage Arena, in the Glass City, hosted this one.

home_lines.text: Toledo opened its home arena in 1976 by beating defending national champion Indiana 59-57, ending the Hoosiers' 33-game winning streak.
Toledo's home building has carried three names: Centennial Hall when it was built in 1976, Savage Hall from 1988 and Savage Arena since 2008, when a $30 million renovation and expansion debuted.
Savage Arena seats 7,300 for basketball, and the court inside is named for Bob Nichols, who went 376-212 as Toledo's coach from 1965 to 1987.
Toledo went 71-10 in its first five seasons in the building now called Savage Arena, and a record 147,203 fans came through in 1980-81.
Savage Arena has hosted more than Toledo basketball since 1976, with Elvis Presley, Frank Sinatra, Elton John and Pearl Jam among the acts that have performed there.

lines.text: Bowling Green played its first men's basketball game on Jan. 8, 1916, a 33-15 loss to the school now known as Eastern Michigan, and finished that first season 3-8.
Bowling Green's 1944-45 team went 24-4 and finished second in the NIT.
Harold Anderson coached Bowling Green for 21 years, compiling a 362-185 record from 1942 to 1963.
Bowling Green teams were known as the Normals, or Teachers, until the school changed its nickname to the Falcons in 1927.
Jim Larranaga led the Bowling Green program for 11 years and was named the MAC Coach of the Year in 1997.
Ohio played its first basketball game in 1907, a 46-9 win over the Parkersburg YMCA.
Ohio reached an NCAA regional final in 1964, when Jim Snyder's Bobcats beat Louisville 71-69 in overtime and No. 4 Kentucky 85-69 before losing to No. 2 Michigan 69-57.
Ohio reached the Sweet 16 as a No. 13 seed in 2012, beating Michigan 65-60 and South Florida 62-56 in Nashville before losing to top-seeded North Carolina 73-65 in overtime.
Ohio won the 2010 MAC tournament as a No. 9 seed, beating Akron 81-75 in overtime in the final, then beat third-seeded Georgetown 97-83 in Providence as a No. 14 seed.
Ohio's most recent NCAA tournament win came on March 20, 2021, when the 13th-seeded Bobcats beat fourth-seeded Virginia 62-58 in Bloomington, Indiana.
Ohio has played in 14 NCAA tournaments, the first in 1960 and the most recent in 2021.
Ohio won the 2021 MAC tournament as a No. 5 seed, beating Kent State, top-seeded Toledo and Buffalo on three straight days in March.
Ohio was the runner-up at the 1941 NIT, beating Duquesne 55-40 and CCNY 45-43 before losing the final to Long Island, 56-42.
Frank Baumholtz, the MVP of the 1941 NIT for Ohio, had his No. 54 retired on Feb. 4, 1995, after a career that included major league baseball with the Reds, Cubs and Phillies.
Jim Snyder coached Ohio from 1949 to 1974, and his teams made seven NCAA tournament appearances and finished with a winning record 21 times in 25 years.
John Groce coached Ohio from 2008 to 2012, going 85-56 with NCAA tournament wins in 2010 and 2012 before leaving for Illinois.
Jeff Boals, a four-year letterwinner and two-year captain at Ohio from 1991 to 1995, is in his eighth season coaching his alma mater after three seasons at Stony Brook.
Ohio hired Jeff Boals on March 17, 2019, and two years later his Bobcats won the MAC tournament and an NCAA tournament game.
Ohio went 15-17 overall and 9-9 in the MAC in 2025-26, its first losing record in seven seasons under Jeff Boals.

home_lines.text: The first men's basketball game at Ohio's Convocation Center in Athens was an 80-70 win over Indiana on Dec. 3, 1968.
The Convocation Center at 95 Richland Ave. in Athens seats 13,080 and doubles as a residence hall and part of Ohio's School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science.
The largest crowd in Convocation Center history is 14,102, for Ohio's game against Bowling Green on Feb. 28, 1970.
Led Zeppelin played a concert at Ohio's Convocation Center in Athens on May 17, 1969.
Ohio's student section at the Convocation Center, the O Zone, dates to the start of the 2001-02 season.
Three of the five largest crowds in Convocation Center history came for Ohio games against Miami, including 13,011 on Jan. 21, 2012.

lines.text: Miami's 1,500th all-time win was a 110-108 overtime victory at Ohio that finished off a 31-0 regular season in 2025-26.
Miami beat Marquette 84-81 in overtime in the first round of the 1978 NCAA tournament.
Miami went into the 1995 NCAA tournament as a No. 12 seed and beat fifth-seeded Arizona 71-62.
Miami reached the 1999 Sweet 16 as a No. 10 seed, beating seventh-seeded Washington 59-58 and second-seeded Utah 66-58.
Miami has retired six men's basketball numbers: 10 for Charlie Coles, 23 for Wayne Embry, 32 for Wally Szczerbiak, 34 for Ron Harper, 44 for Dick Walls and 86 for Darrell Hedric.
Miami in 2025-26 became the fifth Division I program this century to finish a regular season unbeaten, and its 32 wins tied the Mid-American Conference record for a single season.
Miami beat SMU 89-79 in the First Four of the 2026 NCAA tournament as a No. 11 seed.
Miami rose as high as No. 19 in the Associated Press poll during the 2025-26 season.
Charlie Coles won 263 games as Miami's head coach, and the school retired his No. 10 in 2015.
Travis Steele's first four Miami teams went 12-20, 15-17, 25-9 and 32-2, and he was named Mid-American Conference Coach of the Year after the 2025-26 season.
Miami finished 32-2 last season, going 18-0 in the Mid-American Conference before an 87-83 loss to UMass in the league quarterfinals and a 78-56 loss to Tennessee in the NCAA first round.

home_lines.text: Miami drew 10,640 to Millett Hall three times in 2026, for games against Northern Illinois on Jan. 31, Ohio on Feb. 13 and Toledo on March 3.

lines.text: Ball State played its first men's basketball season in 1920-21, going 1-4 across a five-game schedule.
Ball State has made seven NCAA Division I Tournament appearances, in 1981, 1986, 1989, 1990, 1993, 1995 and 2000.
Ball State's only Sweet 16 trip came in 1990, when the 12th-seeded Cardinals beat Oregon State 54-53 and Louisville 62-60.
Ball State's 1990 NCAA Tournament run ended with a 69-67 loss to top-seeded UNLV in the West Regional semifinals, the closest game the eventual national champion played in that tournament.
Ball State's 1988-89 team went a school-record 29-3 and beat Pittsburgh 68-64 in the first round of the NCAA Tournament.
Ball State beat No. 4 Kansas 93-91 at the Maui Invitational on Nov. 19, 2001, on a Patrick Jackson layup with eight-tenths of a second left.
A day after beating Kansas at the 2001 Maui Invitational, Ball State beat No. 3 UCLA 91-73 to earn a title-game date with top-ranked Duke.
Ball State has retired two men's basketball numbers: Ray McCallum's No. 10 and Bonzi Wells' No. 42.
Ball State has won the MAC Tournament seven times, in 1981, 1986, 1989, 1990, 1993, 1995 and 2000.
Ed Butler, who played from 1961 to 1964, leads Ball State with 1,231 career rebounds and had nine games of 24 or more, a single-game total no other Cardinal has reached.
Muncie, the seat of Delaware County, sits on the West Fork of the White River about 50 miles northeast of Indianapolis.
Muncie's natural gas boom began in 1886, and the Ball brothers began glass production there on March 1, 1888.
Muncie is nicknamed Middletown, after the 1929 book Robert and Helen Lynd wrote from their study of the city.
The public television series The Joy of Painting was filmed at WIPB in Muncie.
Garfield creator Jim Davis graduated from Ball State in 1967.
Ball State's teams became the Cardinals after a student vote in which the name drew 234 of 500 ballots to 77 for Hoosieroons.
Ball State wears cardinal and white, and its fight song is titled Fight, Team, Fight.
Ball State's campus landmark is Beneficence, a bronze statue by Daniel Chester French that was dedicated in 1937 and is nicknamed Benny.
Shafer Tower, a 150-foot bell tower with a 48-bell carillon, has stood in the median of McKinley Avenue on the Ball State campus since 2001.
The Ball brothers bought the Indiana Normal Institute in Muncie out of foreclosure for $35,100 on July 25, 1917, and the first 235 students of what became Ball State enrolled on June 17, 1918.
Bonzi Wells, a Muncie Central graduate, left Ball State as the MAC career scoring leader with 2,485 points and went 11th overall in the 1998 NBA draft.
Ray McCallum scored 2,109 points for Ball State from 1979 to 1983, then went 126-76 as the Cardinals' head coach from 1993 to 2000.
David Letterman earned his Ball State degree in 1969, and the university's David Letterman Communication and Media Building opened in 2007.
Chris Capko, a Lakeland, Florida, native who played at Florida and South Florida, was introduced on March 24, 2026, as Ball State's 21st men's basketball head coach.
Ball State plays a 22-game MAC schedule in 2026-27, with two games against each of the other 11 league teams.
Ball State opens MAC play Dec. 2 at Akron, its earliest conference game on the calendar since Nov. 22, 1998.
Ball State won its most recent MAC Tournament title in 2000, beating Miami of Ohio 61-58 in the championship game.

home_lines.text: Worthen Arena seats 11,500 and hosted its first game on Jan. 15, 1992, a Ball State men's and women's doubleheader against Miami University.
Worthen Arena was first called University Arena and was later renamed for John E. Worthen, Ball State's 11th president.
Before Worthen Arena, Ball State played in Irving Gymnasium, a 6,600-seat building that opened in 1962.

lines.text: Buffalo has played men's basketball since 1915 and has been a member of the Mid-American Conference since the 1998-99 season.
Buffalo has made four NCAA Division I tournament appearances, in 2015, 2016, 2018 and 2019, and owns a 2-4 record in those games.
Buffalo's first NCAA Division I tournament win came in 2018, when the 13th-seeded Bulls beat fourth-seeded Arizona 89-68.
Buffalo's 2018-19 team went 32-4, a school record for wins, climbed as high as No. 14 in the AP poll and earned a No. 6 seed in the NCAA tournament.
Buffalo won at No. 13 West Virginia in overtime, 99-94, and at Syracuse, 71-59, during its 32-win season in 2018-19.
Buffalo has won four MAC tournament titles, all in a five-year span: 2015, 2016, 2018 and 2019.
Before its Division I days, Buffalo reached the Elite Eight of the 1957 NCAA Division II tournament, one of six trips the Bulls made to that event between 1957 and 1965.
Buffalo has retired four men's basketball numbers: Jim Horne's 13, Harold Kuhn's 19, Sam Pellom's 50 and Curtis Blackmore's 52.
Sam Pellom, whose No. 50 is retired at Buffalo, went on to play in the NBA for the Atlanta Hawks and Milwaukee Bucks from 1979 to 1983.
Former Buffalo players Jeenathan Williams and Curtis Jones have reached the NBA, Williams debuting with Portland in 2023 and Jones with Denver in 2025.
Nate Oats went 96-43 in four seasons as Buffalo's coach from 2015 to 2019.
Bobby Hurley coached Buffalo for two seasons, went 42-20 and took the Bulls to their first NCAA Division I tournament in 2015.

home_lines.text: Buffalo's home floor opened on Dec. 3, 1982, as Alumni Arena and carried that name until March 2026, when it became Broadview Arena.
Buffalo's Broadview Arena, at 175 Webster Road in Amherst, seats 6,783 for basketball, and only Syracuse has a larger on-campus college basketball facility in New York.
Buffalo's home arena, which opened in 1982, had the largest free-floating hardwood floor in the United States at the time it was built.

lines.text: Central Michigan beat Georgetown 77-75 in the NCAA Tournament on March 15, 1975, when Leonard Drake made two free throws after time had expired.
Central Michigan has played in four NCAA Division I tournaments, in 1975, 1977, 1987 and 2003, and has won three games in them.
The 2002-03 Chippewas went 25-7, setting a Central Michigan record for wins, and beat Creighton 79-73 in the NCAA Tournament before losing to Duke 86-60 in the second round.
Central Michigan won its first Mid-American Conference title in 1975 behind MAC Player of the Year Dan Roundfield, finishing 22-6 under coach Dick Parfitt.
Central Michigan has won the MAC Tournament twice, in 1987 in Toledo and in 2003 in Cleveland.
Central Michigan needed five overtimes to win 109-107 at Toledo on March 4, 1978.
Tommie Johnson scored 53 points for Central Michigan in a 97-68 win at Wright State on Dec. 22, 1987.
Central Michigan's first win over a college opponent came on Jan. 19, 1906, a 20-10 decision over Alma at Normal Hall.
Central Michigan dedicated Finch Fieldhouse with a 60-43 win over Michigan on Dec. 1, 1951.
Mount Pleasant, the seat of Isabella County, sits about 61 miles north of Lansing along US 127.
Oil was found near Mount Pleasant in 1928, and the city known as the Oil Capital of Michigan has an oil drill on its seal and the Oiler as its high school mascot.
Central Michigan University tells prospective students that Mount Pleasant offers 80 miles of the Chippewa River to fish, canoe, kayak and tube.
Mount Pleasant counted 21,688 residents in the 2020 census with a median age of 24.1, and part of the city lies within the Isabella Indian Reservation.
The Ziibiwing Center in Mount Pleasant, just south of Soaring Eagle Casino and Resort, presents exhibits on Anishinaabe culture.
Central Michigan teams were the Dragons and then the Bearcats before assistant football coach Lawrence Sweeney proposed the Chippewas nickname in 1941.
Central Michigan's fight song, The Fighting Chippewa, was written in 1935 by Howdy Loomis.
Central Michigan's student section is the Snake Pit, a name that legend traces to a rival coach's description of playing in the Chippewas' arena.
Central Michigan's Toilet Paper Toss began during the 1982-83 basketball season and was brought back for the first time in 20 years on Jan. 28, 2023.
Central Michigan honors its bond with the Saginaw Chippewa Indian Tribe through Tradition Days, which include tribal drum ceremonies at select football and basketball games.
Dan Majerle, a product of Traverse City High, is Central Michigan's second all-time scorer with 2,055 points and was drafted 14th overall by the Phoenix Suns in 1988.
Central Michigan's Dan Majerle led the bronze-medal 1988 U.S. Olympic team in scoring at 14.1 points per game.
Chris Kaman, a 7-footer from Wyoming, Mich., led the nation with 25 double-doubles for Central Michigan in 2002-03.
The Los Angeles Clippers drafted Central Michigan's Chris Kaman sixth overall on June 26, 2003, making him the highest professional draft pick in school history.
Dan Roundfield, James McElroy and Ben Poquette, teammates on Central Michigan's 1974-75 team, went on to play a combined 30 years in the NBA and ABA.
Andy Bronkema, a native of McBain, Mich., went 278-105 as head coach at Ferris State and won the 2017-18 NCAA Division II national title with a 38-1 team before taking over at Central Michigan.
Andy Bronkema, the 22nd men's basketball coach in Central Michigan history, is in his second season with the Chippewas.
Central Michigan went 10-21 overall and 6-12 in the MAC in 2025-26, Andy Bronkema's first season, finishing 10th in the conference.
Central Michigan's 2026-27 signing class drew from six states and includes 7-foot-2 senior Conrad Luczynski of Bartlett, Ill.
Central Michigan plays a 22-game MAC schedule in 2026-27, a double round robin that sends each of its 11 league opponents to Mount Pleasant once.
The MAC Tournament is set for March 11-13 at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, the city where Central Michigan won its last tournament title in 2003.
Central Michigan's campus in Mount Pleasant and rival Western Michigan's in Kalamazoo are 135 miles apart.
Central Michigan and Western Michigan played their 150th men's basketball game on Jan. 28, 2023, in Mount Pleasant.
Central Michigan's first Mid-American Conference victory was a 70-69 win over Western Michigan on Dec. 30, 1972, with Ben Kelso scoring 29 points.
The Michigan MAC Trophy, created in 2005 by the Michigan Sports Hall of Fame, rewards the best head-to-head record among Central Michigan, Eastern Michigan and Western Michigan in each sport.
Central Michigan and Eastern Michigan met for the 210th time on Jan. 27, 2026, in Mount Pleasant, a series the Eastern Echo called the most frequent matchup in Eastern Michigan history.

home_lines.text: McGuirk Arena, Central Michigan's home floor in Mount Pleasant, has seated 5,300 since the building was reconfigured in 2010.
The floor at McGuirk Arena is Kulhavi Court, named for former Central Michigan trustee John Kulhavi, who pledged $1 million toward the Events Center.
McGuirk Arena drew a record 5,425 on Jan. 28, 2023, when Central Michigan beat Western Michigan 70-69.
Central Michigan's arena opened as Rose Arena on Dec. 1, 1973, a $5.6 million building where James McElroy made the first basket in a 78-70 loss to Michigan State.
A Rose Arena-record 6,455 watched Central Michigan beat Western Michigan 85-71 on Feb. 18, 1987, in a season in which the Chippewas went 13-0 at home.
A bust of broadcaster Dick Enberg, a 1957 Central Michigan graduate, stands in the Events Center atrium in Mount Pleasant, showing the thumbs-up he gave graduates at his 1980 commencement speech.
The practice gym in Central Michigan's Events Center is named for Dick Parfitt, the former Chippewas player and coach who won three Mid-American Conference championships.
David Webber scored 51 points for Central Michigan against Ball State on Feb. 24, 2000, breaking a Rose Arena scoring record that had belonged to Larry Bird.

lines.text: Billy Donlon is in his first season as Eastern Michigan's 31st head coach after four years as associate head coach at Clemson, which reached the Elite Eight in 2024.
Eastern Michigan coach Billy Donlon brought a 155-133 record from nine seasons as a head coach, going 109-94 at Wright State and 46-39 at UMKC.
Western Michigan has made four NCAA Tournament appearances, in 1976, 1998, 2004 and 2014, and has won two games in the event.
Western Michigan's 1976 team went 25-3, beat Virginia Tech 77-67 in overtime in South Bend in the NCAA Tournament and lost 62-57 to Marquette in the Sweet Sixteen in Baton Rouge.
As a No. 11 seed in 1998, Western Michigan beat sixth-seeded Clemson 75-72 in the NCAA Tournament behind 32 points from Rashod Johnson and 24 from Saddi Washington.
Western Michigan went 26-5 in 2003-04, winning the MAC Tournament and earning a No. 11 seed in the NCAA Tournament.
Western Michigan beat Toledo 98-77 in Cleveland for the 2014 MAC Tournament title and drew Syracuse as a No. 14 seed in the NCAA Tournament.
Western Michigan has won six MAC regular-season titles, in 1952, 1976, 1981, 1998, 2004 and 2014.
Western Michigan went 17-0 in 1929-30, an undefeated season in the program's history.
David Kool is Western Michigan's career scoring leader with 2,122 points from 2006 to 2010.
Western Michigan's Ben Handlogten made all 13 of his field goal attempts against Toledo on Jan. 22, 1996, the school record for single-game field goal percentage.
Western Michigan beat Marquette 54-50 in the first round of the 2005 NIT, 29 years after losing to Marquette in the 1976 Sweet Sixteen.
Steve Hawkins coached Western Michigan for 17 seasons from 2003 to 2020 and won 291 games, a total topped at the school only by Buck Read's 345.
Kalamazoo sits halfway between Detroit and Chicago along Interstate 94, about 50 miles south of Grand Rapids.
The Kalamazoo Mall, created in 1959, was the first outdoor pedestrian shopping mall in the United States.
Kalamazoo, home of Western Michigan, is where Orville Gibson incorporated his guitar company on Oct. 11, 1902.
Bell's Brewery was founded in Kalamazoo in 1985 by Larry Bell as the Kalamazoo Brewing Company.
Kalamazoo was platted in 1831 as the village of Bronson, after founder Titus Bronson, and was renamed Kalamazoo in 1836.
The song (I've Got a Gal In) Kalamazoo, named for Western Michigan's hometown, was released in 1942.

Western Michigan teams were the Hilltoppers until 1939, when assistant football coach John Gill won a naming contest with Broncos and gave his $10 prize to the fund to expand what is now Waldo Stadium.
Western Michigan was founded in 1903 as Western State Normal School and was renamed Western Michigan University in 1957.
From 1907 to 1949, a funicular called the Western State Normal Railroad carried students and staff up and down the hill at Western Michigan in Kalamazoo.
Paul Griffin, a 1976 fifth-round draft pick out of Western Michigan, played 480 NBA games from 1977 to 1983.
Basketball Reference lists seven Western Michigan players who reached the NBA or ABA, the most recent being Shayne Whittington in 2015 and 2016.
Don Boven played 195 NBA games from 1950 to 1953 after his Western Michigan career.
Western Michigan counts actors Tim Allen, Terry Crews and Bruce Campbell and singer Luther Vandross among its notable alumni.
Kahil Fennell went 35-29 in two seasons at UTRGV, including 19-14 last season, before Western Michigan hired him in March 2026.
Western Michigan coach Kahil Fennell played at the University of Redlands and spent 10 years in medical device sales before entering coaching, with stops at Louisville and BYU.
Western Michigan went 10-21 in 2025-26 and tied for last in the Mid-American Conference before Kahil Fennell took over the program in March.
Western Michigan opened summer workouts under Kahil Fennell with 14 new players and no returners from last season's roster.
Kahil Fennell's first win as Western Michigan coach was a 99-52 decision over Kalamazoo College on Nov. 5 at University Arena.
Western Michigan plays 22 MAC games this season, facing all 11 league opponents twice in the conference's first full double round-robin.
Western Michigan and the rest of the MAC head to Rocket Arena in Cleveland for the conference tournament March 10-13.

Western Michigan, Central Michigan and Eastern Michigan have played for the Michigan MAC Trophy since the Michigan Sports Hall of Fame created it in 2005 for the best head-to-head record among the three.
Western Michigan holds the men's basketball Michigan MAC Trophy after winning it in 2026, its ninth, against seven for Central Michigan and five for Eastern Michigan.
Western Michigan and rival Central Michigan played their 150th men's basketball meeting on Jan. 28, 2023, in Mount Pleasant.
Western Michigan beat Central Michigan 77-65 at University Arena on Jan. 24, 2026, snapping a four-game Chippewa win streak in the series.

home_lines.text: University Arena, inside Read Fieldhouse on the Western Michigan campus, opened for men's basketball in December 1957 and seats 5,421.
Western Michigan's Read Fieldhouse was named for coach Buck Read, who went 345-169 in 27 years with the Broncos, during a 1963 game against defending NCAA champion Loyola.
A 1994 renovation rotated the court at Western Michigan's University Arena 90 degrees and cut its seating from more than 10,000 to 5,421.
University Arena sits at 2009 Howard St. in Kalamazoo, just north of Stadium Drive and across the street from Western Michigan's football, baseball and softball fields.
Western Michigan's student section, The Zoo, formed in 2003 as the Bronco Brigade and took its current name in 2004.

lines.text: UMass played the first basketball game in program history on Jan. 10, 1900.
The 1933-34 Massachusetts team went 12-0 and was the only undefeated team in men's college basketball that season.
UMass made its first NCAA tournament appearance on March 12, 1962, a 70-50 loss to New York University.
The first postseason win in UMass history came on March 17, 1973, a 78-71 NIT victory over Missouri.
UMass won five straight Atlantic 10 regular-season and tournament titles from 1992 through 1996.
UMass reached its first Elite Eight on March 24, 1995, beating Tulsa 76-51 behind 20 points from Marcus Camby.
UMass beat Syracuse 77-71 in overtime on March 22, 1992, to reach the Sweet 16, where its run ended against Kentucky.
UMass overcame a 22-point second-half deficit to beat Syracuse 81-77 in the 2008 NIT, then lost the championship game to Ohio State, 92-85.
UMass has made nine NCAA tournament appearances, the most recent as a No. 6 seed in 2014.
No. 32 is retired twice at UMass, for Julius Erving and for George Burke, a 1956 second-team All-America selection.
Lou Roe, whose No. 15 is retired at UMass, was the program's first consensus All-American and scored 1,950 career points from 1991 to 1995.
Jack Leaman won 217 games and eight Yankee Conference titles in 13 seasons as UMass coach, the most victories by any coach in school history.
UMass became a full member of the Mid-American Conference on July 1, 2025.
Before the Mullins Center, UMass played in the 4,000-seat Curry Hicks Cage, a 1931 building where home games in its final years were billed as Rage in the Cage.
Amherst was incorporated in 1759 and counted 39,263 residents in the 2020 census, the most of any municipality in Hampshire County.
Amherst is the town where Emily Dickinson was born and lived her whole life, and her home there is now the Emily Dickinson Museum.
Amherst lies 22 miles north of the city of Springfield.
Amherst's 01002 ZIP code is the second-lowest in the continental United States, after Agawam.
Amherst is home to more than fifty working farms and three colleges, and nearly a third of the town's land is permanently conserved.
The W.E.B. Du Bois Library rises 26 stories and 286 feet over the UMass campus in Amherst.
UMass students chose the Minutemen name in a Sept. 28, 1972, vote over Bay Staters, Colonials, Pioneers, Raiders and Statesmen.
UMass admitted its first class in 1863 as Massachusetts Agricultural College, and its early teams were known informally as the Aggies.
UMass wears maroon and white and calls its basketball student section the Militia.
The UMass Minuteman Marching Band counts more than 390 members and is the largest marching band in New England.
Julius Erving averaged 26.3 points and 20.2 rebounds per game at UMass before winning ABA titles in 1974 and 1976 and the 1983 NBA championship.
Marcus Camby left UMass as the 1996 Naismith National Player of the Year with a school-record 336 career blocks and went second overall to Toronto in the 1996 NBA draft.
John Calipari coached UMass from 1988 to 1996, later won the 2012 national title at Kentucky and entered the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2015.
Frank Martin, hired in March 2022 as the 23rd head coach in UMass history, took South Carolina to its first Final Four in 2017.
UMass coach Frank Martin is a Miami native who led Miami Senior High to three straight state championships.
Frank Martin entered his fifth season at UMass with a 64-63 record, including a 20-11 mark in 2023-24.
UMass went 17-16 overall and 7-11 in the league in 2025-26, its first season in the Mid-American Conference, and reached the MAC semifinals as the No. 8 seed.
Danny Carbuccia set a UMass program record with 17 assists in a 2025-26 win over Central Michigan and made the MAC All-Freshman Team.
UMass beat UMass Lowell 72-62 in its Amherst home opener this season behind a career-high 28 points from Junjie Wang.
UMass meets Wake Forest on Dec. 6 at the MassMutual Center in Springfield in the Basketball Hall of Fame Classic, the teams' first meeting since the 1996-97 season.
UMass beat No. 20 Miami (Ohio) 87-83 in the 2026 MAC quarterfinals, its first win over a ranked team since 2013 and the first loss of that season for Miami.
UMass hosts Toledo on Jan. 12 in a rematch of last season's MAC semifinals and closes the regular season at Toledo on March 2.
UMass plays Buffalo twice in MAC play this season, at Buffalo on Jan. 5 and in Amherst on Feb. 23.

home_lines.text: The Mullins Center formally opened on Feb. 4, 1993, and UMass christened it with a 64-59 overtime win over West Virginia.
The Mullins Center in Amherst has a basketball court laid over an Olympic-sized hockey rink.
The Mullins Center in Amherst is named for William D. Mullins, the state representative from Ludlow who proposed a multipurpose arena for the university.
The Mullins Center sits at 200 Commonwealth Avenue on the western edge of the UMass campus, looking out toward the Hadley Hills and the Holyoke Range.
Every seat in the Mullins Center is padded and maroon, and the concession stands in Amherst sell a pickle pizza by the slice.
The Mullins Center in Amherst cost $51 million to build and hosted a Metallica concert on Feb. 15, 1993, less than two weeks after it opened.

akron|kent-state.name: Akron-Kent State
lines: The two campuses sit about a dozen miles apart in Northeast Ohio.

bowling-green|toledo.name: I-75
lines: Bowling Green and Toledo sit about 25 minutes apart on I-75.

miami-oh|ohio.name: Miami-Ohio
lines: Ohio's two oldest public universities, the bricks of Oxford against the bricks of Athens.
